newsitem.title: FRANCE: Five people dead in cult-owned house in Canada.
newsitem.headline: Five people dead in cult-owned house in Canada.

text.p: Five people were found dead in a mystery blaze in a house in Canada owned by a member of a doomsday cult tied to a string of grisly collective suicides and murders, Canadian police said on Sunday.

Independent news channel La Chaine Info (LCI), presenting what it said was an exclusive report, said the three women and two men were all believed to be members or sympathisers of the Order of the Solar Temple.
Pierre Robichaud, a spokesman for Quebec police, told the television that firemen called out police after a blaze in a house at St Casimir near Montreal.
"This house belongs to a member of the OST," he said, adding that one of the five corpses had been partly carbonised in the fire. "So far we have not found arms, we haven't found anything special."

Fifty-three cult members died in a macabre ritual in 1994 in Switzerland and Canada, including guru Luc Jouret. Another 16 charred corpses were found in the French Alps in December 1995 in a murder-cum-suicide.
Robichaud also said that three teenagers, aged 13, 14 and 16 were found lying down in a nearby building, in a "state of confusion, but in good health."

LCI said their parents were believed to be linked to the sect and that cars belonging to sect members were found nearby. It said that Canadian investigators were focusing on the belief that the deaths were linked to the sect.
